t: This is Bond Street, running through the West End from Piccadilly in the south up to Oxford Street in the north. The southern stretch is Old Bond Street and the longer northern part is New Bond Street, though most people don't bother to tell them apart. Since the eighteenth century it has been home to prestigious fashion retailers. The name comes from Sir Thomas Bond, who was Comptroller of the household of Queen Henrietta Maria. Henry Harford, the last proprietor of Maryland, was born here. Anne Brett, a courtier, and the East India Company officer Sir Walter Gilbert both died here.
